Operation.value:
The Hades Compact is a coalition of surviving civilian settlements that endured the destruction of the First War and the horrors of the Awakening. Their name comes from the old Hades defense network, a pre-war emergency system once used to coordinate civilian evacuation and shelter operations across Mors.
The Compact places survival, commerce, and mutual defense above ideology. Its settlements maintain what remains of Mors' industrial infrastructure while trading with other human communities whenever possible.
The Hades Compact does not trust the machines, the old military hierarchy, or those who seek to rule through force. They believe Mors can only survive if its scattered human populations cooperate.

The Scrap Kin are the descendants of Mors' industrial survivors, scavengers, raiders, and displaced workers. They live among the ruins of factories, military installations, and cities destroyed during the First War and the Awakening.
To the Scrap Kin, almost nothing is worthless. Broken machinery becomes weapons. Ruined vehicles become homes. Abandoned factories become settlements. Their communities are rough, heavily armed, and fiercely independent.
They have little patience for the old powers of Mors and even less for anyone who attempts to take what they have claimed. Their brutal reputation has earned them few friends, but their knowledge of the wastelands makes them dangerous enemies.

The Rust Cult emerged from the survivors who fled into the wilderness during the Awakening. They believe the old world was destroyed because humanity placed its faith in machines and technology.
They worship the remnants of the old industrial world as sacred relics while simultaneously fearing the machines that once served humanity. Rusted weapons, broken machinery, and fragments of ancient war machines are treated as objects of spiritual significance.
The Rust Cult is fiercely hostile toward those who embrace the old technological order. Their warriors are hardened by generations of survival in the ruins of Mors, and their hatred of the machines is matched only by their hatred of those who would repeat humanity's mistakes.

The Iron Wraiths are the remnants of Mors' raiders, mercenaries, smugglers, and criminal warbands. When the Awakening shattered the old order, they abandoned any pretense of loyalty and turned the chaos into an opportunity.
Operating from ruined industrial complexes, derelict military facilities, and hidden strongholds, the Iron Wraiths prey upon isolated settlements and traveling caravans. They raid for weapons, ammunition, fuel, medicine, and anything else that can keep their warbands alive.
Some claim the Iron Wraiths helped cause the Second War. Others believe they simply recognized the inevitable collapse before everyone else did. Whatever the truth, they have no intention of allowing peace to return to Mors.

The Autarchs of Iron are the remnants of Mors' former military command structure, forged in the aftermath of the First War and hardened by the catastrophe that followed.
When the Awakening began, the military forces of Mors were among the first to understand the scale of the disaster. Entire command networks collapsed as their own automatroids turned against them, leaving isolated units and surviving officers to fight their way through a war they had never prepared to fight.
The Autarchs believe that humanity can only survive through discipline, hierarchy, and absolute military organization. They have gathered surviving soldiers, officers, engineers, and civilians beneath their command and now seek to reclaim the industrial infrastructure lost during the Awakening.
To their followers, the Autarchs are the last organized defense of human civilization. To their enemies, they are remnants of the old order desperately attempting to restore a world that no longer exists.
